newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria currency board boosts confidence - c.banker.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria currency board boosts confidence - c.banker.

text.p: The currency board system launched in Bulgaria on Tuesday to slow inflation and instil monetary discipline, has already shown signs of raising confidence in the country, the central bank governor said.

"Bulgaria now has a unique chance to stabilise and should not waste it. We see confidence in the government and it is returning to the central bank and the lev," Svetoslav Gavriiski told a news conference.

"The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) is ready for the currency board. There are more than four billion marks in the BNB and the banking system which is enough to cover a 4.4 trillion lev money mass, which now does not exist," he added.

BNB lev liabilities were estimated at 2.2 trillion levs. Under the arrangement, the BNB has pledged to exchange unlimited amounts of marks for levs at a fixed exchange rate with a bid level of 995 levs per mark bid and and an asking level of 1,000 levs.
More than 15 million marks were sold by citizens at the exchange counters opened at the BNB on Tuesday.
"Of 1,500 transactions, only 20 were for buying marks," said the head of the BNB Issue Department Martin Zaimov.
The Issue Department is the core of the currency board operation. It ensures that levs in circulation are matched by foreign exchange reserves. The department is expected to publish a weekly balance.
"With all the international support we have received, Bulgaria starts the board in a very good financial condition," said Gavriiski.

Gross foreign exchange reserves, estimated at around 2.7 billion marks, are the highest since the start of the transition to a market economy while inflation and interest rates are at their lowest since reforms began, said Gavriiski.
May inflation stood at 5.6 percent and the main monthly interest rate fell to around one percent.
Brady bond coupon payments of around $132 million due at end-July will not affect the foreign exchange reserves, said Gavriiski.
He said Bulgaria stood to receive a total of $400 million in the next few weeks under agreements with the International Monetary Fund, the European Union and the World Bank.
The currency board system forbids central bank lending to the government and commercial banks.
Delayed reforms, a chain of bank failures and political instability sent the lev into a freefall earlier this year as inflation soared.
"Fulfilling budget targets will guarantee the successful implementation of the currency board," said Finance Minister Muravei Radev.
Bulgaria's parliament adopted on Saturday an austerity budget for this year which envisages a deficit of 6.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) and a seven percent decline of GDP.
